raw_segments.text: I thought you would cry out again.
Don't speak of it.
Leave off."
Raskolnikov gave a laugh, but rather a forced one.
What?
Silence again, he asked a minute later.
We must talk about something, you know.
It would be interesting for me to know how you would decide a certain problem, as Lebesie
atnikov would say.
He was beginning to lose the thread.
No, really.
I am serious.
Imagine, Sonya, that you had known all Luzhin's intentions beforehand.
Known, that is, for a fact, that they would be the ruin of Katarina Ivanovna and the
children in your self-throne, and since you don't count yourself for anything Polinka,
too.
For she'll go the same way.
Well, if suddenly it all depended on your decision whether he or they should go on living,
that is whether Luzhin should go on living and doing wicked things, or Katarina Ivanovna
should die.
How would you decide which of them was to die?
I ask you.
